title: 2008 AMC 12B Problem 11

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: A cone-shaped mountain has its base on the ocean floor and has a height of \(8000\) feet. The top \(\tfrac{1}{8}\) of the volume of the mountain is above water. What is the depth of the ocean at the base of the mountain, in feet?

solutions.text:
The part above the water is a cone similar to the whole mountain, with volume \(\tfrac{1}{8}\) of the total. Since volume scales as the cube of length, the above-water cone’s height is \(\sqrt[3]{\tfrac{1}{8}} = \tfrac{1}{2}\) of the full height.

So the above-water height is \(8000 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2} = 4000\) feet.

The ocean depth at the base is the submerged height, \(8000 - 4000 = 4000\) feet.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The above-water part is a smaller cone similar to the whole mountain
The volume ratio \(\tfrac{1}{8}\) is the cube of the height ratio; the depth is the total height minus the above-water cone’s height
